source_text: 61.1. '' Quid est , inquit, vobis investigare, conquirere, quisnam hominem fecerit, animarum origo quae sit, quis malorum excogitaverit causas, orbe sit sol amplior an pedis unius latitudine metiatur, alieno ex lumine an propriis luceat fulgoribus luna? Quae neque scire compendium neque ignorare detrimentum est ullum. 2. Remittite haec deo atque ipsum scire concedite, quid quare aut unde sit, debuerit esse aut non esse, supernatum sit aliquid an ortus primigenios habeat, aboleri conveniat an reservari, exuri, dissolvi an repetita integritate renovari. Vestris non est rationibus liberum inplicare vos talibus et tam remota in utilitate curare? 3. Res vestra in ancipiti sita est, salus dico animarum vestrarum, et nisi vos adplicatis dei principis notioni, a corporalibus vinculis exsolutos expectat mors saeva, non repentinam adferens extinctionem sed per tractum temporis cruciabilis poenae acerbitate consumens''.
pass_a_gloss: Objector: why probe who made man, souls’ origin, evils’ causes, sun/moon size—knowing no gain, ignorance no loss. Reply: remit to God what/why/whence; not free to tangle reason in remote curiosities. Stake is salus animarum: unless you apply to dei principis notio, mors saeva waits after bodily release—not sudden wipeout but drawn-out cruciabilis poena.
pass_b_english: 61.1. “What is it to you,” he says, “to investigate and inquire who made the human being, what the origin of souls is, who devised the causes of evils, whether the sun is larger than the world or is measured by the breadth of one foot, whether the moon shines from another’s light or by her own flashes? Things it is no advantage to know and no loss to be ignorant of. 2. Leave these things to God and grant that He Himself know why or whence a thing is, whether it ought to have been or not, whether something is supernaturally produced or has first origins, whether it is fitting that it be abolished or reserved, burned, dissolved, or renewed with recovered integrity. Is it not free for your reasonings to entangle yourselves in such matters and to care for what is so remote from usefulness? 3. Your affair is set in uncertainty—I mean the salvation of your souls—and unless you apply yourselves to the knowledge of God the Prince, a savage death awaits you when you are loosed from bodily bonds, not bringing a sudden extinction but consuming you through a stretch of time by the bitterness of torturing punishment.”

choices.choose: Seek God the Prince for soul-salvation
choices.why: Res vestra… salus animarum; nisi… dei principis notioni

choices.choose: Death as drawn-out penalty without God
choices.why: mors saeva… per tractum temporis cruciabilis poenae

notes: Salvation stakes: apply to God the Prince or face savage lingering death; remit futile inquiries to God.
